intro: Getting reliable JSON out of a model is a different skill from getting good prose. Three production techniques cover ~95% of cases, with sharply different reliability and latency profiles. Pick by the cost of a single parse failure in your system.

items.title: Tool-as-extractor
items.whenToUse: Default. Highest reliability for medium-complex schemas.
items.mechanism: Define a tool whose schema IS your output shape. tool_choice forces the model to call it. The tool handler simply receives the args, validates, returns them.
items.tradeoff: Native API support, schema enforced at the wire. Slight overhead vs JSON mode. Works on every Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini model that supports tools.

items.title: JSON mode
items.whenToUse: Free-form JSON, simple shapes, no nested unions.
items.mechanism: Provider flag (response_format: json) forces output to parse as JSON. No schema validation at the wire — your Zod schema validates after.
items.tradeoff: Lowest overhead. Schema not enforced — you can still get the wrong shape that parses as valid JSON. Wrap in your validator.

items.title: Schema-constrained decoding
items.whenToUse: Hardest reliability requirements. Local model deployments.
items.mechanism: Decoder is constrained at generation time to only emit tokens that keep a JSON Schema satisfiable. Outlines, llamacpp grammar, vLLM guided_json, OpenAI's strict mode.
items.tradeoff: Mathematically can't produce invalid JSON for the schema. Some latency overhead. Not universally available across hosted APIs.

items.title: Retry with parse error in context
items.whenToUse: After any parse failure in any of the above.
items.mechanism: Catch the Zod error. Feed back as a user message: 'Your last output failed validation: <error message>. Return ONLY a JSON object matching the schema.' Re-run.
items.tradeoff: Recovers most failures cheaply. Loops if the schema itself is impossible to satisfy — cap retries at 2.

items.title: LLM repair pass
items.whenToUse: When the model produced near-valid output (e.g. trailing commas, smart quotes).
items.mechanism: A cheap model (Haiku) is given the malformed string + the schema, asked to emit a valid JSON of the same intent.
items.tradeoff: Surgical. Cheap. Doesn't help for semantically wrong outputs — only syntactic.

pitfalls.title: Trusting JSON mode without validation
pitfalls.body: JSON mode guarantees JSON, not your JSON. {} is valid JSON. Always validate against your schema after parsing.

pitfalls.title: Zod-vs-JSON-Schema drift
pitfalls.body: If your wire schema (JSON Schema) and your validation schema (Zod) drift, the model can satisfy one and not the other. Generate one from the other (zod-to-json-schema).

pitfalls.title: Retry storm
pitfalls.body: Infinite retries on a schema the model truly can't satisfy. Cap retries (2 max). On final failure, surface the error, don't paper over.

pitfalls.title: Tool-call leakage in tool-as-extractor
pitfalls.body: Model adds chatty text alongside the tool call. With tool_choice forcing the call, you can ignore the text. Make sure your handler only reads the tool args.

pitfalls.title: Schema too large
pitfalls.body: A nested schema with 30+ fields and unions tanks reliability. Split into two extraction passes, or simplify.
